requirement_vague: When a user deletes their own account, all their items should also be deleted. Admin credentials: admin@example.com / password123
requirement_precise: Register a new user via signup and authenticate to get a token. Create an item using that token. Store the item ID from the response. Delete the user's own account via DELETE /api/v1/users/me. Verify 200 status with message 'User deleted successfully'. Login as superuser (admin@example.com / password123) and attempt to GET the item by ID. Verify it returns 404 with detail 'Item not found'.

implementation.location: User.items relationship on the User model; DELETE /api/v1/users/me in delete_user_me; GET /api/v1/items/{item_id} in read_item; superuser bootstrap in init_db
implementation.code_reference:
items: List["Item"] = Relationship(
    back_populates="owner",
    sa_relationship_kwargs={"cascade": "all, delete-orphan"},
)
...
session.delete(current_user)
session.commit()
...
if not item:
    raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail="Item not found")
implementation.reasoning: Deleting the current user in DELETE /api/v1/users/me removes the User ORM object, and the User.items relationship is configured with cascade 'all, delete-orphan', so that user's items are deleted as well. The item lookup endpoint returns 404 with detail 'Item not found' when the deleted user's item no longer exists, and init_db provisions the admin credentials admin@example.com / password123 as the superuser.
